  • Product feedback loop. Structured objections, feature gaps and lost-deal reasons from sales data,
    delivered to product monthly. Sales becomes a research input, not a complaint channel.

    • Why this matters beyond sales

    layer powers usage-based billing, churn signals and product prioritisation. You present to the whole
    company every quarter, and your backlog is visible to everyone.

    First 30 days: Audit of the current stack and data. Revenue data layer designed and the CRM cleaned

    First 90 days: Forecast model in weekly use. First strategic deal where your prototype or demo was

  • Stay in the engineering culture. You use the company's stack, review practices and security

  • Default to open. Your roadmap, metrics and decisions are visible to the whole company

    LLM-based automation, and the occasional front end.
  • Direct experience with modern GTM tooling (CRM APIs, enrichment and sequencing platforms, call

About the role

We are looking for an accomplished Chain Engineer with a security focus to join our existing highly-skilled global protocol team. You will build and harden the core of the Injective chain, making sure every module, upgrade and integration is safe before it reaches mainnet. You'll work alongside protocol engineers from spec to release, reviewing designs for attack vectors, auditing native chain code and EVM contracts, and building the tooling that keeps the chain secure over time. We're looking for someone who can work autonomously, has a hacker mentality, and thinks like an attacker while building like an engineer.

If you're an autonomous engineer with a strong security mindset who enjoys working with a high degree of ownership, and you're looking to protect and strengthen the financial infrastructure of one of the fastest growing blockchains, this role is for you.

Responsibilities:

  • Execute internal security audits of Injective's Cosmos-SDK modules, including the decentralized orderbook, trade execution coordinator, order matcher, and Layer-2 execution environment

  • Review and audit EVM smart contracts, EVM integrations, and cross-chain bridge and IBC components

  • Partner with senior protocol engineers to build security into new chain features from day one, threat-modeling both technical and economic risks (e.g. oracle manipulation, MEV, liquidation and market-manipulation attacks)

  • Build, maintain, and test hardened core components of the chain (consensus, state management, financial infrastructure), and fix vulnerabilities directly in the codebase

  • Develop security tooling such as fuzzers, invariant and property-based tests, static analysis, and on-chain monitoring and alerting

  • Review chain upgrades and pull requests with a focus on determinism, consensus safety, denial-of-service vectors, and state-machine correctness

  • Write clear, high-quality security reports, both internal and public, and coordinate with external auditors, bug bounty researchers, and partners on findings and disclosure

  • Take part in incident response, and drive post-mortems and remediation when issues arise

  • Research and track the latest blockchain exploits and security developments, and share learnings with the wider team

 

Who you are:

  • Minimum of 3 years' experience as a Blockchain Engineer, with a significant focus on security

  • 5+ years of experience in software security

  • Hands-on experience auditing (internally or externally) DeFi protocols or blockchain core code, with findings you can speak to

  • Solid understanding and proficiency of Golang and/or Solidity

  • Strong knowledge of Go idioms, libraries, and parallel processing, plus the security pitfalls common in Go and Cosmos-SDK chains (non-determinism, panics, unbounded iteration, gas and DoS issues)

  • Strong knowledge of blockchain, DeFi & DEX concepts, consensus mechanisms, CosmWasm contract platform

  • Solid understanding of cryptography primitives, including digital signatures and the hash algorithms used by Ethereum and Cosmos

  • Ability to write clear security reports and explain risk to both technical and non-technical team members

 

Nice to haves:

  • A track record in bug bounties, CTFs, or published audits and CVEs

  • Experience with fuzzing and formal verification tools

  • Prior experience working in trading or at an exchange

  • Knowledge of financial instruments and markets

  • Remote-friendly work environment with flexible hours.

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Equipment

  • Home Office Stipend

  • Opportunity to work on cutting-edge blockchain technology in the finance industry.

  • Collaborative team culture with opportunities for professional growth and development

  • Global team meetups

Building the Future of Open Finance

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

 

The team

Kraken's Consumer Creative & Design team owns end-to-end creative execution for Kraken Consumer and Krak. Our disciplines cover performance ad creative, brand design, motion design, AI video creative and web design. We turn growth strategy into creative that converts across paid, owned and organic surfaces. We work closely with Product Marketing, Performance Marketing, Content & Social, Lifecycle and our regional leads, and we hold the line on brand and messaging quality on everything that ships.

 

The opportunity

As our Staff Brand Designer, you come to the table with a strong design vision and set the visual standard for Kraken. You design static work for launches, campaigns and always-on activity, and you make sure it looks like one brand wherever someone meets it. You can take a brief or proactive idea to a finished, approved asset set, and you're comfortable building a clean, systemized layout in Figma. If you can also model and render a hero 3D asset in Cinema 4D, that's a real bonus.

You report to the Creative Lead, Consumer Creative & Design, who gives you direction, feedback and cover in reviews. This is a senior individual contributor role with no direct reports. Senior here means craft and ownership: you set the bar for brand quality on the team, you build systems others can work from, and you're the person colleagues come to with design questions.

 

What you'll do

  • Design static creative for Kraken across product launches, campaigns, promotions and always-on activity.

  • Apply and extend the Kraken Consumer brand across surfaces, from organic social, lifecycle and web to illustration and foundational projects like key visual updates, keeping everything cohesive and recognizable without making it repetitive.

  • Design initiative-specific work, including a distinct look and partner-branded assets for launches, and purpose-built illustration for go-to-market and product moments.

  • Build scalable systems: Figma component libraries, marketing templates and modular campaign kits with localization-ready layouts, so other designers, other teams and our automated workflows can produce on-brand work quickly.

  • Use AI-assisted production as a core part of how the brand gets made, and know when it speeds the work up and when it doesn't.

  • Bring ideas to briefs rather than executing them literally. Push back with a point of view when a brief is unclear or the idea can be stronger.

  • Version and localize work across markets, languages and formats, with layouts that hold up under translation and market-specific requirements.

  • Partner with Product Marketing, compliance and regional teams to get work approved without losing the idea.

  • Collaborate closely with our motion, web, performance and AI video designers so work travels well across formats.

  • Hold a high craft bar on your own work and give clear, constructive feedback on others'.

 

What you'll bring

  • 7+ years of brand and static design experience at a high-volume in-house team or agency, ideally in fintech, crypto or another regulated category (a competitor or similar company is a big plus).

  • A portfolio that proves it, submitted with your application. Include the brief or objective alongside the work and the result where you're able to share it. We'd like to see brand and static work, an example of work you adapted for multiple formats or markets, and an example of a system or template set that other people built from.   • Expert-level Figma: components, auto layout, variables, and files that are easy to hand off and build on.

  • Strong layout, hierarchy, type and composition that hold up at small sizes and in multiple languages.

  • Hands-on experience with AI-assisted production tools, and good judgment about where they belong in a workflow.

  • Comfort working inside regulatory constraints, including layouts that accommodate risk warnings, disclaimers and market-specific requirements without compromising the design.

  • Working fluency in Adobe CC (Photoshop, Illustrator, and After Effects for light motion).

  • Speed without sloppiness. You're comfortable with fast turnarounds, several review rounds and late changes.

  • A solid instinct for plain language and clear communication: value first, no hype, no jargon.
